PROCEDURE PERFORMED:
Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATIONS:
2.9 cm left lower lobe posterior basal indeterminate lung mass; underlying rheumatoid arthritis. Tissue diagnosis
requested.
MEDICATIONS:
General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
IMAGING / CONFIRMATION:
CBCT; radial EBUS
TECHNICAL DIFFICULTY:
No
LIMITATIONS:
None
TOLERANCE:
Good after intervention
FINDINGS:
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway inspection to the
first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow with fluoroscopy, radial
EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 2.9 cm lesion in the left lower lobe posterior basal. Imaging confirmation used CBCT.
Initial fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated blunted eccentric radial signal. A cone-beam or tomographic spin was
then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship, after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat fluoroscopy was performed. Once tool-in-lesion
or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained included TBNA x4; forceps biopsies x10; brushings x2;
BAL x1. Technical difficulty: No. Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS staging was then performed. Surveyed stations included 11L (5.8 mm), 4L (6.4
mm), 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm). Sampled stations: 11L x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 4L x3 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 7 x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell
block). At the end of the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS:
<5 mL
COMPLICATIONS:
Mild bleeding from biopsy bed, controlled with wedge tamponade and iced saline
IMPRESSION:
Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the left lower lobe posterior basal lesion. Associated EBUS staging
was performed. Minor immediate complication: mild bleeding from biopsy bed, controlled with wedge tamponade and
iced saline.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into
treatment planning

Procedure
Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy with peripheral lesion biopsy

Indication
enlarging pulmonary nodule concerning for primary lung malignancy. Preprocedure CT demonstrated a 8-mm solid RLL target associated with a positive bronchus sign and located about 8 mm from the pleural surface.

Narrative
A time-out was completed and general anesthesia through an 8.5-mm endotracheal tube was established. Conventional bronchoscopy was performed first for airway inspection. The robotic catheter was subsequently introduced and registration to the CT-derived pathway was satisfactory. Ventilation was kept stable during navigation; no special recruitment maneuver was required. Navigation proceeded to the peripheral RB7 medial basal airway. The catheter was locked after the system indicated proximity to the target. mCBCT with 3D reconstruction was used to verify the biopsy trajectory. Tool-in-lesion was confirmed before tissue acquisition; a second spin after sampling showed no immediate pleural complication. Radial EBUS demonstrated an eccentric lesion pattern; the catheter was repositioned toward the maximal ultrasound signal before sampling. Tissue acquisition included 4 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 3 1.1-mm transbronchial cryobiopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (40 mL instilled, 28 mL returned). ROSE was nondiagnostic on the first passes; subsequent samples showed lesional tissue.

Nodal Evaluation
Linear EBUS staging was not performed because there was no clinical indication for nodal staging during this procedure.

Complication
Hemostasis was excellent. The patient tolerated the procedure without immediate complication.

Impression
Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 8-mm solid RLL lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated mCBCT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. No linear EBUS staging was performed. No immediate complication.

The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the segmental level. No active bleeding or endobronchial tumor was seen before robotic navigation.

## Disposition

The patient was transferred to recovery in stable condition after the event resolved.
